reviews.title: Disappointing Experience with ShutEye and Apple’s Refund Policy
reviews.text:
I signed up for ShutEye believing there was a 7-day free trial and intended to try the app before committing to an annual subscription. Instead, I was charged for an entire year. I noticed the charge within two days and promptly requested a refund through Apple, but my request was ultimately denied.

I find this extremely frustrating. I never intended to purchase an annual subscription, and I acted quickly once I realized I had been charged. Being forced to pay for a full year when I barely had any time to use the service feels unfair.

I’m disappointed that no exception was made in this situation. This experience has seriously affected my trust in subscription services and the refund process. I strongly encourage anyone considering ShutEye to carefully review the trial terms and billing details before signing up, so they don’t end up in the same situation.

reviews.title: How Can I Trust the Data When It Defies Physiology?
reviews.text:
I initially found ShutEye useful and relied on it regularly to track my sleep. However, over time the app’s sleep-stage reporting has become increasingly inconsistent and difficult to trust.

For months, the app routinely reported that I was getting 5–7 hours of deep sleep per night. More recently, it began reporting only 0–5 minutes of deep sleep, despite no major change in my sleep habits. At the same time, REM sleep reporting became erratic, and the REM percentage data was eventually removed altogether.

The current data often appears internally inconsistent. On some nights, the app reports less than an hour of total sleep while simultaneously displaying several hours of light sleep. On other nights, it reports implausible amounts of REM sleep. These dramatic shifts make it difficult to determine whether changes reflect my actual sleep patterns or simply changes to the app’s algorithms.

As someone who experiences significant fatigue, morning headaches, and other sleep-related symptoms, I rely on tracking tools to provide reasonably consistent information. Instead, the app’s reporting has become confusing and, at times, appears physiologically impossible.

If sleep-stage calculations or algorithms have changed, users should be informed. Transparency about how sleep stages are measured and how updates affect historical data would go a long way toward maintaining user confidence.

reviews.text: The on the first night, it was good. It was great. In fact I had a lovely sleep. Then on the second night it randomly turned off in the middle of the night. It didn’t wake me up, but I was mad when the music wasn’t playing as I woke up Then the next day it does it again now I’m getting pretty mad because all my family claims to have nothing to do with it then on the fourth day as I’m cooling down getting ready for bed I decide to put some of the music on so I can calm down before bed, then the music randomly turns off, and I can’t put it back on. I exit out of the app and go back into it. I turned on the music, then continued reading my book 5 minutes later the music turns off then I realized that no one had been turning my music off. It was the stupid app the entire time!!! Really what’s wrong with that? How hard is it to just make a good sleep app developer if you Are reading this fix your stupid app!!!!
